title: Custom logistics solutions for complex supply chains
summary: Learn why enterprise supply chains require flexible, purpose-built logistics models. See how GXO helps businesses gain control, scale faster and adapt to change.
body_markdown:
# Standard logistics models were built for a standard world


## Logistics is no longer about moving products efficiently. It is about maintaining performance as market conditions, operational demands and customer expectations continue to change.


## Complex supply chains need control.


## The old assumption


### Scale solves complexity.


More locations. More capacity. More capabilities. More standardized processes.


That can help when needs are predictable. **But enterprise supply chains are rarely standard.**


The more complex the business becomes, the more important it is for the logistics model to fit how the business actually operates.


### The gap:


**Only 19% of leaders feel confident in their ability to scale operations for peak-season swings.***


## The new standard


### The model has to be built around the business.


Enterprise supply chains need logistics models designed around their current state, their growth priorities and the unexpected.


The right model gives leaders more than access to capability. It gives them more ways to **adapt, execute and grow** .


### The need:


**97% of executives say flexibility and the ability to scale quickly are extremely or very important when evaluating 3PLs.***


[*Source: GXO Outsourcing Survey Report – May 2026](https://gxo.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GXO-Outsourcing-Survey-Report-v4-May-2026.pdf)


## What enterprise logistics needs now


### 1. Control


Control over operations, data, service levels and the customer experience.


### 2. Flexibility


The ability to adapt operations, capacity, workflows and technology as needs change.


### 3. Technology choice


A vendor-agnostic approach that applies the right technology to the right operational challenge, without locking the business into one solution.


### 4. Operational expertise


Teams with the experience to design, implement and continuously improve complex logistics operations.


### 5. Purpose-built fit


A logistics model designed around the business, not a standard model the business has to work around.

## **The takeaway**


### The right logistics model should not force the business to adapt around it.


It should give the business more control, more flexibility and more room to grow.
